### L1 review (#34994) · 2026-11-17T23:47Z

L1: ACCEPT
Head-sha: b4162eabbf700d4b4a6b0780f0ea209b8042ee10

`check-governed-merges --branch` at this head reads GOVERNED, Tier S (the `.github/workflows/**` split, 4 files, +184 / −30). That matches claim amendment 6964076137 and the PR body's patched tier line. The seat's PASS contract review on this head is owed before the area queues it. This verdict does not ready the PR.

#### Must-fix
None.

#### Should-fix
None.

#### What I checked
- **Mechanism.**
  - `GIT_HTTP_LOW_SPEED_LIMIT` and `GIT_HTTP_LOW_SPEED_TIME` are git's documented environment overrides for `http.lowSpeedLimit` and `http.lowSpeedTime`. A workflow-level `env:` reaches every step's process, including `actions/checkout`'s git, which the dev read as inheriting `process.env`, with `fetch()` inside `retryHelper.execute`.
  - The diagnosis holds together. The pre-pack orphan list has no `index-pack`, the watchdog's `sleep` PID kept climbing, and sideband `remote:` progress kept the log growing. So a silence bound cannot fire, and a byte-rate bound can. The local curl-28 abort during `remote: Compressing objects` is the direct reproduction.
  - The margins are as the body states. 120 s is 8× the slowest measured pre-pack wait (14.7 s), and 1000 B/s is orders of magnitude below a healthy receive.
- **No budget moves.** Every `timeout-minutes` and job wall is untouched, so #29980's slow-transfer replay is not re-opened. The 60 s silence watchdog stays as the backstop.
- **`fetch-history.sh`.**
  - The defaults are exported only when unset, so the workflow values win (pinned by the `preset 5 7` case).
  - `current_phase` reads only complete lines. A trailing partial write, detected through `tail -c 1 | od -c`, falls back to the previous key, and an empty log prints nothing.
  - The phase line prints only on a change of key.
  - The header now records why #34561's reading failed.
- **`lint-eslint` at depth 1.** Its three steps are `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`; `eslint.config.mjs` has no `child_process`), `check:engine-double-contract` (no `child_process`, no git) and `lane-verdict.mjs` (no git). None reads history. `check:slot-lookup` runs in `lint-scoped-slot-corpus` (lint.yml:4372), which keeps `fetch-depth: 0`. The six "same reason as" pointers now name `lint-repo-tooling`, whose checkout carries the merge-base reason. `git grep` at this head finds no pointer left at the ESLint job's checkout.
- **Self-test.** The new cases pin the env reaching git, the talk-then-curl28 retry with no stall warning, the live phase lines, one workflow `env:` block per file matching the script's defaults (a parity guard against drift), and `lint-eslint` with no `fetch-depth`. The ablations (7 FAIL with the exports made plain assignments, and exactly 1 FAIL for lint.yml `120` → `60`) show those pins bite. CI's `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` runs `check:fetch-history` green.
- **Scope and shape.** All four paths are inside claim 6962740145's surface, and `governed-surface-guard.yml` is untouched, per the route ruling. `Fixes #34994`, Clause-② `no` and Metadata-protocol `none` match the claim. `skip-changeset` is right because `.github/**` and `scripts/ci/**` ship in no package. The body states measured readings with job ids and queries, and names the 4 NOT MEASURED dist-reading families with their reason.
- **CI on this sha.** 54 runs, all completed: 37 success, 17 skipped, 0 failed. Every checkout and fetch in this PR's own run ran under the new env, which is the live positive control the body names.

#### Notes
- N1 (nit): `current_phase` takes the text before the first colon of any complete line as the phase. So `From https://…` prints as `From https`, and a colon-less ref-update line (` * branch … -> FETCH_HEAD`) prints whole. These are diagnostic lines only, and few for this fetch's refs.
- N2 (nit, reflow): the self-test header leaves one overlong comment line ("…that each phase prints as it starts. A real stalled transfer cannot be ordered on"). The lint.yml note above the `breaking-change` checkout wraps early ("cross-referenced: shallow").
- N3: the residual risk is a healthy request whose server pre-pack phase passes 120 s. It would be cut and retried, and only fail after three such draws. The post-landing 24 h re-measure on #34994 is the right reading for it, and its expected signature (`curl 28` then `Waiting N seconds` or `Attempt 2 of 3`) is stated in the body.
- N4: `lint-eslint` keeps the 25-minute CHECKOUT BUDGET at depth 1. The new note says so, and resizing it belongs with #22034.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b4162eabbf700d4b4a6b0780f0ea209b8042ee10`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .github/workflows/ci.yml, .github/workflows/lint.yml + scripts/ci/fetch-history.sh, scripts/ci/fetch-history.selftest.sh

Inputs read: card #34994 (body and all 5 comments: claim 6962740145, triage network reading 6962889910, PHASE 1 report 6963324497, PHASE 2 report 6964012625, claim amendment 6964076137); PR #35032 (body, 4-file list, the net diff `origin/main...b4162eabbf`, +184 / -30, both comments: L1 6964430715 and the review claim 6964461600); the 54 check-runs on the head. Both workflow files, the script and the files they cite were read in the head tree. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

No published schema, export or accept set moves. The diff changes CI behaviour only, in five ways.

- **Every git HTTP request in ci.yml and lint.yml aborts under 1000 B/s for 120 s: right.**
  - Each file has exactly one top-level `env:` block (ci.yml:200, lint.yml:227) carrying both values.
  - No job or step re-sets or clears either variable. Neither file has a `container:` job, a reusable-workflow `uses:`, a `docker run` or an `env -i`, so nothing sits outside the workflow env.
  - The transfers it reaches, counted in the head tree: 21 `actions/checkout@v7` steps in ci.yml and 12 in lint.yml; the five `fetch-history.sh` steps (ci.yml:825, 1157, 3897, 4180, 4363); the two inline `git fetch` lines of the eager-closure step (ci.yml:5207, 5213); and the fetches inside `select-gate-families.sh`, `select-shard-packages.sh`, `build-schemas.ts` and `check-skill-frame-freshness.mjs`.
  - Neither workflow pushes, clones another repository or uses submodules or LFS, so no upload path is exposed to the bound.
- **`lint-eslint` checks out at depth 1: right.** See ④.
- **`fetch-history.sh` prints new lines (the bound, once; `fetch-history: +Ns PHASE` per phase): right.** Its only reader is its own self-test, which pins them.
- **`fetch-history.sh` exports the two defaults when unset: right.** A workflow's values win, and the `preset 5 7` case pins that.
- **Not covered, by the route taken: `governed-surface-guard.yml`'s merge_group checkout (depth 0, 20 min) and every other workflow.** The PHASE 1 report measured 0 stalls on it in 48 h. This is a residual, not a defect of this diff.

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is right. `.github/**` and `scripts/ci/**` ship in no package, and the diff touches no package file. `Check Changeset` concluded success on the head.

Clause-②: no. The PR body, the claim and the diff agree: no published schema, export or accept set changes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Route (PHASE 1 open question 1): answered, A.** The diff is route A exactly: the env block in both workflows, the script's defaults and phase lines, `lint-eslint` at depth 1, no step budget or job wall changed.
- **`governed-surface-guard.yml` (PHASE 1 open question 2): answered, A (not touched).** The diff leaves it alone.
- **Tier (PHASE 2 open question): answered, Tier S**, by claim amendment 6964076137. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` concluded success on the head.
- **Dev deviations (the HTML-comment trailer, `Fixes #34994` as the body's first line):** not a contract matter. `PR-body guards` concluded success.
- **SQL push-down: not applicable.** The diff has no data access, id materialisation or join.
- One provenance note for the seat: the card carries no seat comment recording the route ruling. I read it only through the PHASE 2 report ("Route A, as the seat ruled") and the amendment. The diff matches the dev's recommended option on both PHASE 1 questions, so nothing is left open; the adopting seat is the one that knows the ruling was given.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**The five questions the review was asked**

1. **Does the env reach every git transfer? Yes.** The inventory in ① is complete for both files. A workflow-level `env:` is in the process environment of every `run:` step and every JS action, and git reads both variables directly, ahead of `http.lowSpeedLimit` / `http.lowSpeedTime` config. One thing I did not verify first-hand: that `actions/checkout@v7` wraps its fetch in a 3-attempt retry and passes `process.env` to git. That rests on the dev's read of the v7 source (PHASE 1 report) and matches how earlier majors behave; the action is not vendored in this tree.
2. **Can 1000 B/s for 120 s false-fail a slow but healthy transfer? Not one that is receiving a pack.** A healthy receive runs at MiB/s, four to five orders above the limit. The exposed case is a healthy server that takes over 120 s to start the pack: that attempt is cut and retried, and the step fails only after three such draws.
   - The evidence against that case is stronger than the comments say. Over 48 h, the whole `fetch-history` step ran p99 88 s (n 12,368) and the full-ref checkout p99 120 s (n 10,296), so the pre-pack wait alone is under 120 s for well over 99% of healthy runs.
   - The live control held: every checkout and fetch in this PR's own CI ran under the bound, and all 54 check-runs completed with 37 success, 17 skipped, 0 failed.
   - The stall side has no CI proof and cannot have one. It rests on the dev's local abort (rc 128, `curl 28`) while `remote: Compressing objects` was still streaming, which is the right reproduction.
3. **Does depth 1 break a `lint-eslint` step that needs history? No.** The job at the head has four steps after checkout, none conditional on the event.
   - `Setup workspace`: node, pnpm and the store cache; no git read.
   - `pnpm lint`: `eslint . --no-inline-config`. `eslint.config.mjs` and `packages/eslint-plugin/src` contain no `child_process`, `execSync` or `spawnSync`.
   - `check:engine-double-contract`: imports `node:fs`, `node:path`, `node:url` and local parsers; its only `origin/main` mentions are in comments.
   - `lane-verdict.mjs`: no git.
   - The slot-lookup ratchet the old note cited runs in `lint-scoped-slot-corpus` (lint.yml:4372), which keeps `fetch-depth: 0`. `Lint · ESLint` concluded success on the head at depth 1.
4. **Does the self-test pin the new behaviour? Yes.** It pins: the defaults reaching git (`1000 120`); a preset surviving; a `talk-then-curl28` attempt retried to green with no silence warning; the live phase line for server and receive phases; one `env:` block per workflow equal to the script's defaults; and `lint-eslint` with no `fetch-depth`. `run_case` strips both variables with `env -u` before each case, so the cases still test the script's own defaults when the suite runs under the workflow env. The dev's two ablations (7 FAIL, 1 FAIL) show the pins bite. `check:fetch-history` runs unconditionally in `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, which concluded success.
5. **Does a retry path still exist? Yes, for the two paths that stalled.** `fetch-history.sh` retries any non-zero attempt, so exit 128 gets attempts 2 and 3; the 60 s silence watchdog still returns 124 into the same loop. `actions/checkout` has its own retry (see 1). The remaining fetches have no retry and never had one; under the bound a stall there fails in about 2 minutes instead of running to the job wall, so nothing regresses.

**Sentence-by-sentence agreement**

- ci.yml's block comment agrees with the tree and the card: 48 steps is 29 merge_group/main plus 19 PR-event; the budgets are 8 to 25 minutes; both retry counts match.
- lint.yml's block comment agrees: 20 full-history checkouts is 10 plus 10.
- The six "same reason as" pointers now name `lint-repo-tooling`, whose checkout carries the merge-base reason. No pointer to the ESLint checkout is left.
- The script header agrees with the code: the exports are conditional, `current_phase` reads complete lines only, and the phase line prints on a change of key.
- Worst-case timing fits the smallest budget. Two cut attempts plus a healthy third is about 2 x 125 + 45 + 60 to 90 s, roughly 355 to 385 s against the 8-minute `Plan Test Core shards` step. Three cut attempts end at about 420 s with the named `::error::`, still inside it.

**Nits**

- N1 (nit) — the margin sentence overstates its evidence. "The slowest healthy wait for the pack is ~15 s" (both workflow comments and the script header) and the PR body's "holds a 6.5x slowdown" rest on one local sample per fetch shape, on git 2.43 through a proxy, and assume the pre-pack wait scales with the whole transfer. In a 2026-11-03-style slowdown, where 11.9% of fetches ran over 10 minutes, some slow but healthy attempts would be cut and retried. That is no worse than today: a cut costs 2 minutes, and three in a row is in the range of the 0.42 to 1.51% the budgets already fail. The post-landing 24 h re-measure is the right control; it should also count `curl 28` lines on runs that then went green.
- N2 (nit) — the 8-minute fetch budget has about 95 to 125 s of headroom for the two-cuts-then-healthy case. A third attempt slower than that is ended by the budget, not by the script. Fine today (p99 88 s); worth knowing if that budget is ever cut.
- N3 (nit) — the workflow comments name two retries and say nothing of the unretried fetches (ci.yml:5207, 5213 and the script-internal ones), which are bounded but fail on the first cut. The heading is true; the retry sentence is just narrower than "every git transfer".
- N4 (nit) — lint.yml's `History fetch self-test` step comment (around line 3354) still lists only the #34561 cases. It is not wrong, only short of the new ones.
- N5 (nit) — L1's N1 and N2 stand as accepted deviations: `current_phase` keys a colon-less line whole and `From https://…` as `From https`; one self-test header line is overlong and one lint.yml note wraps early.

All five are comment or diagnostic text with no effect on correctness. A fix would move the head; a follow-up or leaving them is fine.
